text: From the study by Mann et al. (lying):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline how the averages were calculated on the data about the number of words the
participants used in their descriptions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe what was found from these averages.

text: From the study by Loftus and Pickrell (false memories):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the revised eyes test results from Group 1 (AS/HFA) and Group 4 (IQ matched
controls).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
What did Baron-Cohen et al. conclude about social and non-social intelligence in adults with
autism spectrum disorders?

text: From the study by Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe how the kittens’ eyes were tested for normal functioning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why this test was important.

text: In the study by Held and Hein (kitten carousel) it was important to know that the kittens’ eyes were
still functioning normally.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what the participants were told about the purpose before they began the experiment.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why it was necessary to hide the true purpose during the experiment.

text: In the study by Milgram (obedience), the participants were not told the true purpose of the
experiment until the end.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two of the ‘administrative routines’ that the guards were asked to perform.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe what happened to these routines over the course of the study.

text: From the study by Haney, Banks and Zimbardo (prison simulation):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what ‘diffusion of responsibility’ predicts.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain whether the results of the study support diffusion of responsibility.

text: Piliavin et al. studied subway Samaritans.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Name the two social norms which Tajfel suggested the participants applied.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain how there could be negative consequences for society from one of these social
norms.

text: In the study by Tajfel (intergroup categorisation) he says that the motivation of social behaviour is
complex and that social norms are important.
From the study by Bandura et al. (aggression):
Describe two categories of non-imitative aggression that were observed. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the results for euphoria obtained by self report.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one other way in which the euphoria data were collected and state whether these
results were the same as the self-report results, or different.

text: In the study by Schachter and Singer (emotion) three experimental groups were compared in
relation to euphoria and the data were collected in several different ways.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline two dreams from participants who had a mixture of horizontal and vertical eye
movements.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how these eye movements were explained.

text: In the study by Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreaming), participants were asked to describe
their dreams.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline the procedure for this task.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify one of the tasks that the route task was compared to, and explain why it was important.

text: In the study by Maguire et al., taxi drivers were asked to describe a route through London.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe how Eve Black stayed hidden for so long.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one piece of evidence from a test which showed that Eve Black and Eve White were
different.

text: From the study by Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder):

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what is meant by ‘systemising’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the results for systemising from the study.

text: Billington et al. studied empathising and systemising.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the control group.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe how the participants in the control group were recruited.
